title: Wait for a page condition
description: Wait, bounded, for one condition on the page instead of polling dsagent.page.observe: the revision to change (sinceRevision), a target to appear, go, become enabled or become disabled (targetId + expectedRevision), text to show or to go, the address to change, the page to settle, a surface to…
guidance: Wait, bounded, for one condition on the page instead of polling dsagent.page.observe: the revision to change (sinceRevision), a target to appear, go, become enabled or become disabled (targetId + expectedRevision), text to show or to go, the address to change, the page to settle, a surface to close (surfaceId from pageSurfaces), the sign-in wall to clear, or a file the page saves to finish downloading. Returns met or timed-out with the latest revision; then observe with baseRevision. Read-only: no idempotency key, nothing is dispatched. Use it after an action whose receipt said pageSettled false, after a navigation the page performs itself, while the person signs in (authentication-cleared), or before acting on a panel that is still opening. A timed-out wait is not a failure of the page: read it and decide. A page the browser is not drawing is refused with PAGE_NOT_RENDERED before waiting: dsagent.page.focus, then wait again. A tab showing no web page yet keeps its pageContextId; reads refuse it (PAGE_NOT_WEB_DOCUMENT): wait until url-changed. authentication-cleared is never met there.

inputSchema.description: The page, the condition and its bound.

pageContextId.description: Page context from dsagent.page.open, dsagent.pages.list or a receipt's destinationPageContextId.

until.description: revision-changed: the page revision differs from sinceRevision. target-present / target-absent: the target (targetId at expectedRevision, from the latest observation) is visible / gone. target-enabled / target-disabled: the target is shown and takes input / is shown disabled (its observed state disabled: a disabled control or aria-disabled), for a Next or Publish button that enables once an upload or a required field is done. text-present: the page shows the text anywhere in the document, frames included. text-absent: the page no longer shows the text anywhere (a "uploading" or "saving" note that goes away). url-changed: the address differs from the one at the start of the wait. settled: the page went quiet (no control-relevant mutations, its own requests finished). surface-closed: the surface with surfaceId is no longer open. authentication-cleared: the sign-in or verification wall is gone. download: a file the page started saving since your latest action on it (or since the wait began) finished downloading, or the browser stopped it (download.state says which); use it after a click whose page saves the file later: an export it builds first, a "your download will start" countdown, a document the server renders.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait at most; 10000 by default.

sinceRevision.description: With revision-changed: the revision you hold.

targetId.description: With target-present / target-absent / target-enabled / target-disabled: a target id a reply gave you.

expectedRevision.description: With targetId: the revision it was published at.

text.description: With text-present / text-absent: the words the page should show (or stop showing), as it prints them.

surfaceId.description: With surface-closed: the surface from pageSurfaces.

outputSchema.description: Whether the condition was met within the bound, and where the page is now.

pageContextId.description: Page context from dsagent.page.open, dsagent.pages.list or a receipt's destinationPageContextId.

outcome.description: met: the condition held; timed-out: it did not within timeoutMs (read the page and decide; it is not an error).

waitedMs.description: How long the wait took for its condition, not counting the read of the page that names the revision after it.

revision.description: The page revision when the wait ended (a met wait reads the page again if its condition did not), current enough to act at; pass it as baseRevision to the next observe. Absent when text-present was met without a page read: observe next.

url.description: The page address as last read.

change.description: With sinceRevision: whether the latest revision differs from it.

authentication.description: With authentication-cleared and timed-out: the wall still standing (status, kind).

download.description: With download, once the page started one: the file as the browser saved it. A timed-out wait with state in_progress: the file is still arriving; wait again rather than clicking again.

state.description: complete: saved locally; in_progress: still arriving; interrupted: the browser stopped it (a server error, a refused or cancelled download): the file was not saved.

fileName.description: The name it was saved under, with the numbering the browser gives duplicates; never a folder.

filePath.description: With complete only: the confirmed absolute local path. Explicitly report this saved location to the person.

sizeBytes.description: Its size in bytes (the bytes announced while it is still arriving).

mimeType.description: The type the server sent it as.

interruptReason.description: With interrupted: why the browser stopped it (SERVER_BAD_CONTENT, NETWORK_FAILED, USER_CANCELED...).

siteResponsiveness.description: Present only while something is wrong with how websites answer this task's tab; absent when they answer normally. site-slow: the website itself is slow, stalled, failing, rate-limiting or unreachable while other websites in the same tab answer normally, so it is not a browser or Agent fault. local-network-slow: every website is slow alike, so it is the person's network or proxy. Either way: do not switch browsers, reload the extension or repeat actions faster; tell the person once which website is slow, then wait (dsagent_page_wait) and read again. DSphere never changes its own timeouts because of it.

verdict.description: site-slow: the website is the problem; local-network-slow: the person's network or proxy is.

reason.description: What is wrong: slow answers (median wait 3 s or more), requests waiting over 10 s, failing requests (5xx or connection errors), rate limiting (HTTP 429), or the website cannot be reached.

host.description: Host name of the tab's website; never a path or query.

medianWaitMs.description: Median time the website took to start answering over the last 20 s; absent when no request answered.

stalledRequests.description: The website's requests waiting more than 10 s without an answer (long polls excluded).

failedRequests.description: The website's requests that failed in the last 20 s.

sampledRequests.description: The website's requests counted in the last 20 s.

controlMedianWaitMs.description: Median wait of the other websites the same tab loaded over the last 60 s (the comparison); absent when none answered.

hint.description: One sentence on what to do.
